$comment: This file is the ONE statement of the shape, and `scripts/check-runbooks.mjs` reads it rather than
restating it — a checker carrying its own copy of the field list is a second statement that drifts,
and the field it would stop requiring is whichever one somebody added last.
It is deliberately NOT a JSON Schema document. Validating one needs a validator, this workspace has
no JSON Schema dependency, and adding one for eleven fields would put a supply-chain surface behind a
documentation gate. Instead each field names a `kind`, the checker implements the kinds, and a kind it
does not implement is REFUSED by name (`runbook-schema-construct-unimplemented`) rather than skipped
— so the schema cannot grow a rule that nothing enforces, which is the failure mode of a schema a
The front-matter FORMAT is as narrow as the schema: one `key: value` per line between two `---` lines
at the very top of the file, no continuation lines, no nesting, lists comma-separated, an empty list
written `(none)`. Narrow because the parser is then the format, and a runbook that is almost valid
YAML is refused with the line number rather than parsed into something nobody meant.

id.why: Held equal to the file stem, so a renamed file cannot keep an id other documents cite.

title.why: What this runbook is for, in the words an index would show.

unit.why: Who wrote it, so a question about a step has somewhere to go.

trigger_kind.why: A runbook with no trigger is a document nobody will ever open at the right moment. `alert` is the only kind that requires a non-empty `alerts` list, which is what makes an orphan runbook detectable rather than a matter of opinion.

trigger.why: What is true when somebody should be reading this. A sentence and not a label, because the reader is deciding whether they are in the right document.

first_action_heading.why: The heading in THIS file holding the first thing to do. Checked against the file's own headings, which is the acceptance line's "every heading a check references must exist" — the front matter's claim is machine-checked rather than prose beside the document.

first_action.why: The first action in one sentence, readable before the document is. At 2am the first step is the only part that gets read properly.

owner.why: An F07 role and never a person: no name of a person is in this repository (brief rule 10) and no contact detail is on file (`Y13-oncall`).

escalation.why: What escalating means here. For most of these the honest answer is that there is nobody to escalate to, and saying so is the point — a field left blank reads like a field nobody filled in.

alerts.why: The alert ids this runbook answers, held against `ALERT_REGISTRY` in BOTH directions: an id here that the registry does not define, and an alert whose registry entry points at this file while this list omits it.

env.why: The environment variables a reader is told to set or read, each held against `packages/config/src/env.ts`. Declared rather than only detected because a variable discussed in prose is still one somebody will go looking for.
